claim: The schedule IR represents a forward pass as tasks connected by monotonically incremented counters and static-threshold waits, with per-SM serial queues and page allocation as explicit schedule state.
caveats: Current documented scope is more mature for dense Llama-family forward than dynamic batching or MoE.

claim: The persistent decode path keeps a device program containing buffers, counters, instructions, per-SM queues, scratch, and an abort flag across a multi-token single-launch execution.
caveats: A design record must still state which model stages the generated program includes.

claim: The whole-forward design uses a persistent device interpreter with per-SM instruction sequences and specialized controller, loader, consumer, and storer roles.

locator.symbol: megakernel device entry and role dispatch

caveats: Instruction and resource schedules are model and architecture specific.

claim: The controller manages a shared-memory page abstraction so non-overlapping intermediate lifetimes can reuse resident scratch across instructions.
applicability: instruction programs with analyzable buffer lifetimes
caveats: Page size and resident resource pressure constrain portability.

claim: One persistent phase-interpreter launch can consume a prompt, execute embedding and all forward phases, compute LM-head argmax, and feed generated tokens back into the next step inside an in-kernel generation loop.
caveats: The implementation is specialized and does not imply general sampling or arbitrary model support.

claim: The same device phase logic also has a per-phase launch mode, creating a clean same-code contrast between one persistent launch and ordinary multiple launches.
caveats: The per-phase path is a comparison/debug mode, not a strict MegaKernel execution boundary.

claim: Machete computes barrier indices from tile coordinates at compile time and keeps compact wait/signal formulas beside a flat tile instruction stream.
caveats: Runtime waits and instruction fetch still have costs even when formulas are precomputed.

claim: Machete provides a host-side readiness scheduler that simulates compiled barrier formulas and emits currently ready tiles instead of only broad producer-then-consumer waves.
applicability: static graphs where ordering can reduce runtime stalls
caveats: This is compile-time ordering, not a fully dynamic device ready queue.

claim: Mirage MPK separates persistent worker and scheduler roles, maintains worker queues plus scheduler event queues, and dispatches tasks after dependency events fire.
caveats: Scheduler SM, queue, atomic, and fence overhead must be part of the cost model.

claim: The runtime header exposes tasks, events, queue state, and worker/scheduler configuration as an explicit device execution contract.
caveats: Individual task handlers and model builders determine the actual fused stage boundary.

claim: Fleet groups workers on the same XCD onto tiles of the same GEMM so they can reuse weights in the XCD-local L2 rather than treating all CUs as a flat pool.
caveats: The mapping is not a generic recommendation for single-die GPUs.

claim: Workers aggregate task completion in XCD-local event counters and only publish a global event when the XCD-local share completes, reducing cross-chiplet synchronization traffic.
caveats: Memory-scope primitives and thresholds are AMD/topology specific.

claim: MegaTritonKernel builds a Python task graph and lowers registered task implementations, scheduling metadata, barriers, and model code into a generated Triton execution program.
caveats: Support varies by task/operator and backend; inspect the generated model path before claiming whole-model coverage.

claim: The optimized path uses a model-specific cooperative MegaKernel across the fixed transformer layer schedule, while separate prefill implementations provide a useful boundary contrast.
caveats: Model, batch, and phase specialization limit reuse.

claim: The Transformer token-generation device program executes multiple transformer layers, attention/MLP/residual work, and cross-layer collective logic inside one NKI invocation.
caveats: NKI invocation semantics and hardware are not CUDA launches, but they are an equivalent device-resident substrate.

claim: The SM100 MegaMoE kernel fuses and overlaps expert-parallel dispatch, FP8×FP4 linear1, SwiGLU, linear2, and combine using symmetric multi-process memory.
caveats: Only the MegaMoE subpath has this boundary; ordinary DeepGEMM kernels are not all MegaKernels.

claim: A dedicated test path exercises MegaMoE correctness and performance separately from ordinary GEMM tests.
caveats: Use the test's exact topology, dtype, and shape contract when interpreting results.

claim: FlashInfer exposes both mega and split MoE EP backend families under the same higher-level subsystem, so backend selection must be recorded at design-path granularity rather than labeling the entire repository.
caveats: Each backend may cover different dtypes, hardware, and stage boundaries.

claim: Mixture-of-Kittens implements deterministic MoE training forward and backward MegaKernels with configurable communication-SM allocation and schedule reuse across both directions.
caveats: NVL72 topology and training-specific state are core assumptions.

claim: One cooperative persistent kernel assigns dispatch, scheduler, compute, combine, and gather worker roles; readiness signals connect received tokens to expert batches and results to combine.
caveats: Role counts and readiness thresholds must be tuned to topology and token distribution.

claim: The Ascend dispatch_mega_combine path coordinates AIC/AIV waves and task queues to cover reorder, dispatch, two grouped matmuls, activation, combine, and unpermute in a device-side MoE pipeline.
applicability: Ascend A5 and documented A2/A3 variants
caveats: Vendor license restrictions and device semantics must be retained in downstream use.

claim: The Pallas Fused EP MoE device program covers routing, all-to-all scatter, expert FFN, all-to-all gather, optional shared expert, and accumulation inside the fused invocation.
caveats: Pallas collective and TPU execution semantics differ from CUDA cooperative kernels.

claim: The main CUDA MegaKernel covers embedding, 28 transformer layers, and final normalization, but LM-head vocabulary projection and argmax execute in a separate kernel path.
caveats: This is near-whole-model, not one-launch whole generation.

claim: StreamEP overlaps dispatch, two persistent grouped-GEMM kernels, and combine through per-tile/per-token readiness signals on caller-owned compute and communication streams rather than one cooperative kernel.
caveats: It targets the same overlap problem but is a multi-kernel alternative by launch semantics.

claim: An 81-kernel CUDA Graph with Programmatic Dependent Launch reconstructs most of a matched persistent Hazy MegaKernel's scheduling effect while retaining separate kernel boundaries.
caveats: It is intentionally not a single persistent device kernel.

claim: DeepEP provides expert-parallel dispatch and combine communication primitives; without expert FFN stages inside the same device invocation it is communication infrastructure rather than a complete MegaMoE.
caveats: Downstream projects may embed or extend these primitives into a strict MegaMoE path.

claim: Mirage's KDA adapter treats a faithful in-MPK per-task measurement as the promotion authority and demotes a standalone green-context benchmark to a directional pre-filter because standalone ranking can fail to transfer.

locator.symbol: What KDA is / faithful in-MPK measure

applicability: agent-driven kernel replacement inside a persistent runtime
caveats: The concrete grid, metric, and correctness thresholds are Mirage-task specific; transfer the evaluation principle, not those constants.
